items.rationale: The model keeps nothing between sessions and the API does not carry history over; memory exists only if your program saves it and sends it again. Believing the model remembers on its own shows M3.

Call 1 input is 2,000 + 100 = 2,100. Call 2 re-sends all of that plus the 500-token result (the tool request itself is ignored): 2,600. Total 2,100 + 2,600 = 4,700. An answer of 2,600 counts only the final context and forgets that each call is billed for its whole input.
Each call re-sends the whole context, so cost multiplies, and recall degrades as context grows (context rot). A bigger window does not remove either problem. Retrieval fetches only the relevant page.

items.answer: Your application (the program around the model) does; the model only requests the operation.
items.rationale: A client-side tool means the model only emits a request; your own code runs it against storage you control. Saying the model reads or writes the files itself shows M4.

items.answer: A student's training status, because it must survive between sessions and is not in the manuals.
accepted: which machines a student is trained on
items.rationale: Notes hold facts about this user or this run that must outlive the context and are not in any document to retrieve. Manual content such as a temperature setting is the opposite: it is in the manuals and is retrieved on demand.
